# gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gzip-header/

## Expand description

A library to decode and encode headers for the
[gzip format](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-gzip.html).
The library also contains a reader absctraction over a CRC checksum hasher.

A file in the gzip format contains a gzip header, a number of compressed data blocks in the
[DEFLATE](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-deflate.html) format, and ends with the CRC32-checksum
(in the IEEE format) and number of bytes (modulo `2^32`) of the uncompressed data.

The gzip header is purely a set of metadata, and doesn’t have any impact on the decoding of the
compressed data other than the fact that `DEFLATE`-encoded data with a gzip-header is
checked using the CRC32 algorithm.

This library is based on the gzip header functionality in the
[flate2](https://crates.io/crates/flate2) crate.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Crc](https://docs.rs/struct.Crc.html)
- A wrapper struct containing a CRC checksum in the format used by gzip and the amount of bytes input to it mod 2^32.
- [CrcReader](https://docs.rs/struct.CrcReader.html)
- A reader that updates the checksum and counter of a `Crc`struct when reading from the wrapped reader.
- [GzBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.GzBuilder.html)
- A builder structure to create a new gzip header.
- [GzHeader](https://docs.rs/struct.GzHeader.html)
- A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Extra](https://docs.rs/enum.ExtraFlags.html)- Flags
- Valid values for the extra flag in the gzip specification.
- [File](https://docs.rs/enum.FileSystemType.html)- System - Type
- An enum describing the different OS types described in the gzip format. See http://www.gzip.org/format.txt (Additionally, the Apple(19) value is defined in the zlib library).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_gz_header.html)- gz_ - header
- Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.

---

# gzip-header 1.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest

# gzip-header

A library to decode and encode headers for the [gzip format](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-gzip.html).
The library also contains a reader absctraction over a CRC checksum hasher.

A file in the gzip format contains a gzip header, a number of compressed data blocks in the [DEFLATE](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-deflate.html) format, and ends with the CRC32-checksum (in the IEEE format) and number of bytes (modulo `2^32`) of the uncompressed data.

The gzip header is purely a set of metadata, and doesn't have any impact on the decoding of the compressed data other than the fact that `DEFLATE`-encoded data with a gzip-header is checked using the CRC32 algorithm.

This library is based on the gzip header functionality in the [flate2](https://crates.io/crates/flate2) crate.

Currently requires rust 1.32 and newer.

# License

Like the non-C parts of `flate2-rs`, `gzip-header` is distributed under the terms of both the MIT license and the Apache License (Version 2.0),

See LICENSE-APACHE, and LICENSE-MIT for details.

# crc32fast - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crc32fast/^1.5/

## Expand description

Fast, SIMD-accelerated CRC32 (IEEE) checksum computation.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#simple-usage)Simple usage

For simple use-cases, you can call the [ hash()](https://docs.rs/fn.hash.html) convenience function to
directly compute the CRC32 checksum for a given byte slice:

`let checksum = crc32fast::hash(b"foo bar baz");`[§](https://docs.rs#advanced-usage)Advanced usage

For use-cases that require more flexibility or performance, for example when
processing large amounts of data, you can create and manipulate a [ Hasher](https://docs.rs/struct.Hasher.html):

```
use crc32fast::Hasher;
let mut hasher = Hasher::new();
hasher.update(b"foo bar baz");
let checksum = hasher.finalize();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#performance)Performance

This crate contains multiple CRC32 implementations:

- A fast baseline implementation which processes up to 16 bytes per iteration
- An optimized implementation for modern `x86`using`sse`and`pclmulqdq`instructions

Calling the [ Hasher::new](https://docs.rs/struct.Hasher.html#method.new) constructor at runtime will perform a feature detection to select the most
optimal implementation for the current CPU feature set.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Hasher](https://docs.rs/struct.Hasher.html)
- Represents an in-progress CRC32 computation.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [hash](https://docs.rs/fn.hash.html)
- Computes the CRC32 hash of a byte slice.

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# car-a2a

Agent2Agent (A2A) v1.0 bridge for [Common Agent Runtime](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car).

## What it does

Exposes a CAR runtime as an A2A-compliant agent so peer agents — built on any A2A SDK (Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, .NET, or one of the Rust crates) — can discover the runtime via an Agent Card and submit work as A2A Tasks.

A2A is the Linux Foundation's open protocol for agent-to-agent interoperability. The full spec lives at [https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/).

## Mapping

| A2A | CAR |
|---|---|
| Agent Card | Manifest of registered tools + host metadata |
| Task | One-shot wrapper around an `ActionProposal` |
| Message (parts) | Free-form input from the peer; structured `data`parts become tool calls |
| Artifact | One per `ActionResult`returned by the runtime |
| `TaskState`SUBMITTED → WORKING → COMPLETED/FAILED | Lifecycle of `Runtime::execute` |

## Surface

| Item | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `A2aDispatcher` | Transport-neutral JSON-RPC dispatcher for the 11 A2A methods |
| `AgentCardSource` | Trait the dispatcher calls to (re)build the agent card on demand |
| `TaskStore`/`InMemoryTaskStore` | Pluggable task persistence |
| `message_to_proposal` | Compile an A2A `Message`into a CAR`ActionProposal` |
| `action_results_to_artifacts` | Convert a `ProposalResult`into A2A`Artifact`s |

## Methods supported

- `message/send`
- `tasks/get`
- `tasks/list`
- `tasks/cancel`
- `tasks/pushNotificationConfig/{set,get,list,delete}`
- `agent/getAuthenticatedExtendedCard`

Out of scope for this prototype:

- `message/stream`and- `tasks/resubscribe`(Server-Sent Events)
- gRPC and HTTP+JSON/REST transport bindings
- Outbound A2A client calls — for those, use `a2a-protocol-client`or`a2a-client`from crates.io.

## Status

Prototype. The dispatcher is exercised by unit tests against an in-process `Runtime` and `InMemoryTaskStore`. It is not yet wired into `car-server-core::handler::run_dispatch` or fronted by an HTTP listener — embedders pick the transport.

## Example

```
use Arc;
use ;
use Runtime;
let runtime = new;
let store = new;
let card_factory = new;
let dispatcher = new;
// A peer's JSON-RPC request:
let result = dispatcher
    .dispatch
    .await
    .unwrap;
```

# car-engine

Core runtime engine for the [Common Agent Runtime](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car).

## What it does

The engine receives action proposals from a model, builds a dependency DAG, and executes actions
concurrently where possible. It handles validation, idempotency, timeouts, retries, and state
rollback on abort. Integrates with `car-policy` for rule enforcement and `car-eventlog` for
audit logging.

## Usage

```
use ;
use ActionProposal;
// Register tools and execute proposals
let runtime = new;
let result = runtime.execute.await?;
```
## Crate features

- DAG-based concurrent execution
- Result caching with `ResultCache`
- Rate limiting with `RateLimiter`
- Capability-based tool access control
- Checkpoint/restore for crash recovery

Part of [CAR](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car) -- see the main repo for full documentation.

# bevy_clerestory - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bevy_clerestory/0.1.1/bevy_clerestory/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#bevy_clerestory)bevy_clerestory

A Bevy plugin for window state persistence and multi-monitor utilities.

[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

Originally created as a mechanism to restore the `PrimaryWindow` to its last known position when launching - the way you expect an app to work. I quickly discovered that on my `MacBook` Pro with Retina display (scale factor 2.0) and my external monitor (scale factor 1.0), there were numerous issues with saving/restoring positions across differently-scaled monitors.

The first discovered issue is that winit uses the scale factor of the focused window from which you launch the application. And if the target monitor for the app has a different scale factor, then that will get factored into the size and position calculations resulting in something you definitely don’t want.

`bevy_clerestory` plugin works around this issue by using winit directly to capture actual monitor position/size/scale and comparing it to the target position/size for the window and does the conversions correctly.

Windows has similar scale factor issues, plus additional quirks like invisible window borders that prevent precise placement. Linux X11 has its own quirks with window manager keyboard shortcuts not firing position events. This plugin now supports macOS, Windows, and Linux (X11 and Wayland) with workarounds for platform-specific issues (see [Platform Support](https://docs.rs#platform-support) for details).

Future directions include comprehensive multi-monitor lifecycle support.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use bevy::prelude::*;
use bevy_clerestory::WindowManagerPlugin;
fn main() {
    App::new()
        .add_plugins(DefaultPlugins)
        .add_plugins(WindowManagerPlugin)
        .run();
}
```
For a complete interactive example with fullscreen mode switching, run:

`cargo run --example restore_window`[§](https://docs.rs#api)API

This crate exposes several types for working with monitors and windows beyond the plugin itself. See [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/bevy_clerestory) for full API documentation.

[§](https://docs.rs#monitors-resource)`Monitors` Resource

Query available monitors sorted by position:

- `monitors.at(physical_x, physical_y)`– Find the monitor containing a position (physical pixels)
- `monitors.by_index(index)`– Get monitor by sorted index
- `monitors.first()`– Get the first monitor (index 0)
- `monitors.closest_to(physical_x, physical_y)`– Find the closest monitor to a position (physical pixels)

[§](https://docs.rs#monitorinfo)`MonitorInfo`

Information about a single monitor: `index`, `scale`, `position`, and `size`.

[§](https://docs.rs#currentmonitor-component)`CurrentMonitor` Component

Automatically maintained on all managed windows. Query it to get monitor info and effective mode:

```
fn my_system(q: Query<(&Window, &CurrentMonitor), With<PrimaryWindow>>) {
    let (window, monitor) = q.single();
    println!("Monitor {}, scale {}", monitor.index, monitor.scale);
    println!("Effective mode: {:?}", monitor.effective_window_mode);
}
```
- `monitor.index`,- `monitor.scale`,- `monitor.position`,- `monitor.size`– Monitor info (via- `Deref<Target = MonitorInfo>`)
- `monitor.effective_window_mode`– The actual window mode, even when- `window.mode`is stale (e.g., macOS green button fullscreen reports- `Windowed`but the window is actually fullscreen)

[§](https://docs.rs#plugin-configuration)Plugin Configuration

- `WindowManagerPlugin`– Uses executable name for config directory
- `WindowManagerPlugin::with_app_name("name")`– Custom app name
- `WindowManagerPlugin::with_path(path)`– Full control over state file path
- `WindowManagerPlugin::with_persistence(mode)`– Set persistence behavior for managed windows

[§](https://docs.rs#multi-window-support)Multi-Window Support

Add `ManagedWindow` to any secondary window to opt it into save/restore:

```
use bevy_clerestory::ManagedWindow;
commands.spawn((
    Window {
        title: "Inspector".into(),
        ..default()
    },
    ManagedWindow {
        name: "inspector".to_string(),
    },
));
```
Each managed window gets the same restore treatment as the primary window — scale factor compensation, position clamping, and platform workarounds.

Control what happens when windows are closed with `ManagedWindowPersistence`:

- `RememberAll`(default) — closed windows keep their saved state for next launch
- `ActiveOnly`— only currently open windows are persisted

```
use bevy_clerestory::ManagedWindowPersistence;
use bevy_clerestory::WindowManagerPlugin;
app.add_plugins(WindowManagerPlugin::with_persistence(ManagedWindowPersistence::ActiveOnly));
```
See `examples/restore_window.rs` for a complete interactive example.

[§](https://docs.rs#state-file-format)State File Format

The state file uses a versioned v2 schema:

- `version: 2`
- `entries: [{ key, state }, ...]`

All spatial values (position, size) are stored in **logical pixels**, making them independent
of monitor scale factor. On restore, values are converted to physical pixels using the target
monitor’s live scale factor.

`key` is typed (`Primary` or `Managed("<name>")`), so the primary window and a managed
window named `"primary"` are distinct and unambiguous.

Legacy state files (unversioned and v1) are still accepted on read and migrated to v2 on save.

[§](https://docs.rs#version-compatibility)Version Compatibility

| bevy_clerestory | Bevy |
|---|---|
| 0.1 | 0.19 |

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-support)Platform Support

| Platform | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | ✅ Tested | Native hardware with multiple monitors at different scales |
| Windows | ✅ Tested | `VMware`VM with multi-monitor, different scale factors |
| Linux X11 | ✅ Tested | Position and size restoration with keyboard snap workaround |
| Linux Wayland | ✅ Tested | Size + fullscreen only (Wayland cannot query/set position) |

**Note on Windows testing**: Windows support has been tested in a `VMware` virtual machine with multiple monitors at different scale factors. Native Windows installations may behave differently - if you encounter issues, please open an issue with details about your monitor configuration.

**Note on Linux support**: Linux support has been tested on KDE Plasma (Asahi Linux on Fedora). X11 includes a workaround for keyboard snap shortcuts (Meta+Arrow) that don’t fire position events ([winit #4443](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/4443)). Wayland has an inherent limitation: clients cannot query or set window position, so only size and fullscreen state can be restored. If you encounter issues, please open an issue with details about your distribution, desktop environment, and monitor configuration.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags-platform-workarounds)Feature Flags (Platform Workarounds)

This plugin includes workarounds for known issues in winit and Bevy. Each workaround is behind a feature flag, and **all are enabled by default**.

This design allows:

- **Easy testing of upstream fixes**- disable a workaround to verify an upstream fix works
- **Opt-out flexibility**- if a workaround doesn’t suit your setup, you can exclude it
- **Minimal code when not needed**- platform-specific workarounds are compiled out on other platforms

[§](https://docs.rs#available-feature-flags)Available Feature Flags

| Feature | Platform | Issue | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workaround-winit-4341` | Windows | [winit #4041](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/4041) | DPI drag bounce fix |
| `workaround-winit-3124` | Windows | [winit #3124](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/3124) | DX12/DXGI fullscreen crash fix |
| `workaround-winit-4443` | Linux X11 | [winit #4443](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/4443) | Keyboard snap position fix |
| `workaround-winit-4440` | Windows, macOS, Linux X11 | [winit #4440](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/issues/4440) | Multi-monitor scale factor compensation |

[§](https://docs.rs#disabling-workarounds)Disabling Workarounds

To test without a specific workaround (e.g., to verify an upstream fix):

```
# Disable all workarounds
cargo run --example restore_window --no-default-features
```
In your `Cargo.toml`, you can selectively enable features:

```
[dependencies]
bevy_clerestory = { version = "0.1", default-features = false, features = ["workaround-winit-4341"] }
```

[§](https://docs.rs#technical-details)Technical Details

[§](https://docs.rs#the-problem)The Problem

On macOS with multiple monitors that have different scale factors (e.g., a Retina display at scale 2.0 and an external monitor at scale 1.0), Bevy’s window positioning has issues:

-
`Window.position`is unreliable at startup`Window.position`is`Automatic`(not`At(position)`), even though winit has placed the window at a specific physical position.
-
**Scale factor conversion in**: When you modify`changed_windows``Window.resolution`, Bevy’s`changed_windows`system applies scale factor conversion if`scale_factor != cached_scale_factor`. This corrupts the size when moving windows between monitors with different scale factors.
-
**Timing of scale factor updates**: The`CachedWindow`is updated after winit events are processed, but our systems run before we receive the`ScaleFactorChanged`event.

[§](https://docs.rs#the-solution)The Solution

This plugin uses winit directly to capture the actual window position at startup,
compensates for scale factor conversions, restores `Window.position`,
`Window.resolution`, visibility, and monitor state across monitors.

The plugin automatically hides the window during startup and shows it after positioning is complete, preventing any visual flash at the default position.

See the `custom_app_name` example for how to override the `app_name` used in the path
(default is to choose the executable name).

See the `custom_path` example for how to override the full path to the state file.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Current](https://docs.rs/struct.CurrentMonitor.html)- Monitor
- Component storing the current monitor and effective window mode.
- [Managed](https://docs.rs/struct.ManagedWindow.html)- Window
- Marks a window entity as managed by the window manager plugin.
- [Monitor](https://docs.rs/struct.MonitorInfo.html)- Info
- Information about a single monitor.
- [Monitors](https://docs.rs/struct.Monitors.html)
- Sorted monitor list, updated when monitors change.
- [Window](https://docs.rs/struct.WindowManagerPlugin.html)- Manager - Plugin
- The main plugin. See module docs for usage.
- [Window](https://docs.rs/struct.WindowRestoreMismatch.html)- Restore - Mismatch
- Event fired when the actual window state doesn’t match what was requested.
- [Window](https://docs.rs/struct.WindowRestored.html)- Restored
- Event fired when a window restore completes and the window becomes visible.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Managed](https://docs.rs/enum.ManagedWindowPersistence.html)- Window - Persistence
- Controls what happens to saved state when a managed window is despawned.
- [Platform](https://docs.rs/enum.Platform.html)
- The display platform, detected once at startup and inserted as a `Resource`
- [Window](https://docs.rs/enum.WindowKey.html)- Key
- Typed identifier for persisted window state.

# car-reason

Code reasoning engine for [Common Agent Runtime](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car). Adaptive, graph-driven, learning.

## What it does

Instead of a hardcoded "diagnose → suggest → explain" pipeline, reasoning actions are **skills in the memgine graph**. The graph's spreading activation and success/failure tracking determine which actions to run, in what order, routed to which models. As outcomes accumulate, the routing improves without code changes.

## Usage

```
use ;
use ReasoningSession;
let inference = new;
let mut memgine = new;
// Seed the default reasoning skills
seed_defaults;
let memgine = new;
let session = new;
let result = session.reason.await?;
println!;
for s in &result.suggestions
println!;
```
## Where it fits

A higher-level capability over `car-memgine` + `car-inference` + `car-ast`. Used by the `car` CLI's diagnostic / fix slash commands and by `.claude-plugin/agents/reason.md`.

## Inference handle abstraction (Parslee-ai/car#189)

`ReasoningSession` does not depend on the concrete `InferenceEngine`. It holds an `Arc<dyn ReasoningInferenceHandle>` — the narrow trait surface this crate exports in [ handle.rs](https://docs.rs/src/handle.rs).

The trait extends [ car_inference::InferenceHandle](https://docs.rs/car-inference/src/handle.rs) (which provides

`generate` + `embed`) with three reasoning-specific methods:| Method | Used for | In-process impl | Daemon impl |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generate_tracked(req)` | Per-action `InferenceResult`(trace_id, model_used, latency_ms) | `InferenceEngine::generate_tracked` | daemon's `infer`JSON-RPC method |
| `find_model_by_name(name)` | Tier-picker checks whether a candidate model is registered before naming it | `unified_registry.find_by_name` | cached `models.list_unified`snapshot |
| `record_inferred_outcomes(action_results)` | Post-session learning loop (writes inferred outcomes for each action's trace) | takes the engine's tracker write lock | best-effort no-op (no `outcomes.resolve_pending`endpoint yet — follow-up) |

This lets callers pick the inference backend at runtime:

```
// In-process (offline dev, tests, CI)
let inference:  =
    new;
// Daemon-routed (`car-server` running locally; shared hot weights + accumulated profiles)
let inference:  =
    new;
```
`cmd_reason` in `car-cli` does the runtime selection — probes the daemon with a cheap `models.list` RPC and falls back to an embedded engine if unreachable. See `car-rs/crates/car-cli/src/daemon_handle.rs` for the daemon-side `ReasoningInferenceHandle` impl.

**Why a new trait instead of growing  InferenceHandle.**

`InferenceHandle` (added in #188 for memgine) is intentionally minimal — `generate` + `embed` — because memgine is reachable from many crates and a wide trait surface multiplies daemon-proxy work for every implementor. `ReasoningInferenceHandle` extends it with the three methods car-reason actually uses, keeping the lower-level trait clean while still letting daemon impls compose: `DaemonInferenceHandle` implements both, with one shared WebSocket connection.

# wipe_daemon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wipe-daemon/0.1.1/wipe_daemon/

## Expand description

The wipe local daemon: an `axum` server that exposes the board over HTTP/WS
and serves the embedded human UI. Started by `wipe serve`.

Collaboration remains git-only; this daemon is a *local* convenience for the
human UX. It records each served project in a machine-wide registry so the UI
can list every board you have opened.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AppState](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html)
- Shared server state.
- [Project](https://docs.rs/struct.ProjectEntry.html)- Entry
- One registered project.
- [Serve](https://docs.rs/struct.ServeConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration for a `wipe serve`invocation.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_projects.html)- projects
- List all registered projects that still have a `.wipe`board, annotating each with its current board name.
- [serve](https://docs.rs/fn.serve.html)
- Start the daemon and serve until the process is stopped (Ctrl-C).

[), stable ID formatting (](https://docs.rs/store/index.html)

`id`[).](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)

`error`Every mutation of a `.wipe` directory in the entire project MUST go through this
crate so that serialization stays deterministic (stable key order, trailing

# dingo_proto - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/dingo-proto/0.2.0/dingo_proto/

## Expand description

A high-performance, no_std-compatible DNS packet parser focused on speed and safety.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use dingo_proto::Message;
let packet = [
     // Header
     0x12, 0x34,             // ID = 0x1234
     0x01, 0x00,             // Flags: RD=1 (standard query with recursion desired)
     0x00, 0x01,             // QDCOUNT = 1
     0x00, 0x00,             // ANCOUNT = 0
     0x00, 0x00,             // NSCOUNT = 0
     0x00, 0x00,             // ARCOUNT = 0
     // Question section
     0x07, b'e', b'x', b'a', b'm', b'p', b'l', b'e',
     0x03, b'c', b'o', b'm',
     0x00,
     0x00, 0x01,             // QTYPE = A (1)
     0x00, 0x01,             // QCLASS = IN (1)
];
Message::parse(&packet).unwrap();
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Header](https://docs.rs/struct.Header.html)
- [Label](https://docs.rs/struct.LabelIter.html)- Iter
- Iterator over the labels of a DNS domain name.
- [Message](https://docs.rs/struct.Message.html)
- A zero-copy DNS message.
- [Message](https://docs.rs/struct.MessageOwned.html)- Owned
- An owned DNS message with all sections parsed.
- [Name](https://docs.rs/struct.Name.html)
- A zero-copy borrowed DNS domain name.
- [Name](https://docs.rs/struct.NameOwned.html)- Owned
- An owned DNS domain name.
- [Question](https://docs.rs/struct.Question.html)
- A zero-copy DNS question entry.
- [Question](https://docs.rs/struct.QuestionIter.html)- Iter
- Iterator over the questions in a DNS message.
- [Question](https://docs.rs/struct.QuestionOwned.html)- Owned
- An owned DNS question entry.
- [Resource](https://docs.rs/struct.ResourceRecord.html)- Record
- A zero-copy DNS resource record.
- [Resource](https://docs.rs/struct.ResourceRecordIter.html)- Record - Iter
- Iterator over resource records in a DNS message section.
- [Resource](https://docs.rs/struct.ResourceRecordOwned.html)- Record - Owned
- An owned DNS resource record.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- Possible errors that may occur when parsing a DNS packet
- [QR](https://docs.rs/enum.QR.html)
- [Response](https://docs.rs/enum.ResponseCode.html)- Code
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.Type.html)
- From section 3.2.2 of RFC 1035

# car-planner 0.32.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/car-planner/0.32.0

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/car-planner/0.32.0/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

# car-planner

Proposal scoring and search for [Common Agent Runtime](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car).

## What it does

Sits between the model and `car-engine`: scores N candidate proposals using static verification + cost estimation, picks the best, and provides fallback ordering for replan scenarios.

Inspired by MARS (budget-aware MCTS) — uses `verify()` + `simulate()` as the evaluation function, **not LLM calls**. Pure Rust, zero inference cost.

## Usage

```
use ;
let planner = new;
let candidates = vec!;
let ranked = planner.rank;
let best = &ranked; // highest score first
```
## Where it fits

If you already have N candidate proposals, use this directly. If you also need CAR to *generate* the candidates via inference, use `car-active-planner`, which composes inference with this ranker. Exposed to FFI consumers as the standalone `rank_proposals` function.

# car-mcp 0.32.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/car-mcp/0.32.0

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/car-mcp/0.32.0/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

MCP (Model Context Protocol) server library — transport-agnostic dispatch for exposing CAR capabilities to MCP-aware clients.

Two transports use this crate today:

- **stdio**—- `car-mcp-server`binary, one client per process. Suitable for Claude Desktop / Cursor / Claude Code's- `--mcp-config`and any other client that follows the MCP spec's stdio framing. See [- `transport::stdio_loop`].
- **HTTP-streamable**—- `car-server`daemon endpoint, many concurrent clients sharing the same- `Runtime`/ policy chain / eventlog. Implemented in- `car-server-core`against the same [- `Server::handle`] entry point. (Phase 2 stage 4b — pending.)

Both share the same `Server::handle(Request) -> Option<Response>`
pure function, so transports stay separable from protocol logic.

## Why a library crate

Originally this lived in `car-mcp-server`'s `main.rs` as a
self-contained binary. v0.8 + the external-agent work made it
clear MCP needs to be a first-class daemon surface so every
external client (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, custom GPTs) gets
CAR's tools through the same governance layer. Extracting the
dispatch logic into a library lets the daemon embed it without
shelling out to a subprocess. See
`docs/proposals/external-agent-detection.md` (Phase 2 stage 4b).

---

# car-memgine 0.32.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/car-memgine/0.32.0

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/car-memgine/0.32.0/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

# car-memgine

Graph-based memory engine for the [Common Agent Runtime](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car).

## What it does

Memory is a graph. Nodes represent facts, skills, conversations, identity, and environment. Edges encode relationships: Supersedes, DependsOn, RelatedTo, Triggers, TemporalNext. Skills are learned procedures stored as graph nodes with trigger edges, matched via spreading activation, and tracked for success/failure. Supports distillation from event log traces.

## Usage

```
use ;
let engine = new;
engine.ingest_fact.await?;
let hits = engine.retrieve.await?;
```
## Crate features

- `metal`-- Apple Silicon GPU acceleration (via car-inference)
- `cuda`-- NVIDIA GPU acceleration (via car-inference)
- `ast`-- AST-aware skill representation via- `car-ast`

Part of [CAR](https://github.com/Parslee-ai/car) -- see the main repo for full documentation.

# gzip-header 1.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/1.1.0

# gzip-header

A library to decode and encode headers for the [gzip format](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-gzip.html).
The library also contains a reader absctraction over a CRC checksum hasher.

A file in the gzip format contains a gzip header, a number of compressed data blocks in the [DEFLATE](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-deflate.html) format, and ends with the CRC32-checksum (in the IEEE format) and number of bytes (modulo `2^32`) of the uncompressed data.

The gzip header is purely a set of metadata, and doesn't have any impact on the decoding of the compressed data other than the fact that `DEFLATE`-encoded data with a gzip-header is checked using the CRC32 algorithm.

This library is based on the gzip header functionality in the [flate2](https://crates.io/crates/flate2) crate.

Currently requires rust 1.32 and newer.

# License

Like the non-C parts of `flate2-rs`, `gzip-header` is distributed under the terms of both the MIT license and the Apache License (Version 2.0),

See LICENSE-APACHE, and LICENSE-MIT for details.

---

# gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/1.1.0/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/gzip_header/

## Expand description

A library to decode and encode headers for the
[gzip format](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-gzip.html).
The library also contains a reader absctraction over a CRC checksum hasher.

A file in the gzip format contains a gzip header, a number of compressed data blocks in the
[DEFLATE](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-deflate.html) format, and ends with the CRC32-checksum
(in the IEEE format) and number of bytes (modulo `2^32`) of the uncompressed data.

The gzip header is purely a set of metadata, and doesn’t have any impact on the decoding of the
compressed data other than the fact that `DEFLATE`-encoded data with a gzip-header is
checked using the CRC32 algorithm.

This library is based on the gzip header functionality in the
[flate2](https://crates.io/crates/flate2) crate.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Crc](https://docs.rs/struct.Crc.html)
- A wrapper struct containing a CRC checksum in the format used by gzip and the amount of bytes input to it mod 2^32.
- [CrcReader](https://docs.rs/struct.CrcReader.html)
- A reader that updates the checksum and counter of a `Crc`struct when reading from the wrapped reader.
- [GzBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.GzBuilder.html)
- A builder structure to create a new gzip header.
- [GzHeader](https://docs.rs/struct.GzHeader.html)
- A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Extra](https://docs.rs/enum.ExtraFlags.html)- Flags
- Valid values for the extra flag in the gzip specification.
- [File](https://docs.rs/enum.FileSystemType.html)- System - Type
- An enum describing the different OS types described in the gzip format. See http://www.gzip.org/format.txt (Additionally, the Apple(19) value is defined in the zlib library).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_gz_header.html)- gz_ - header
- Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.

- [GzHeader](https://docs.rs/struct.GzHeader.html)
- A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Extra](https://docs.rs/enum.ExtraFlags.html)- Flags
- Valid values for the extra flag in the gzip specification.
- [File](https://docs.rs/enum.FileSystemType.html)- System - Type
- An enum describing the different OS types described in the gzip format. See http://www.gzip.org/format.txt (Additionally, the Apple(19) value is defined in the zlib library).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_gz_header.html)- gz_ - header
- Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.

# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/gzip-header/1.1.0/src/gzip_header/lib.rs.html

# gzip_header/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! A library to decode and encode headers for the
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//! [gzip format](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-gzip.html).
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! The library also contains a reader absctraction over a CRC checksum hasher.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! A file in the gzip format contains a gzip header, a number of compressed data blocks in the
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! [DEFLATE](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-deflate.html) format, and ends with the CRC32-checksum
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! (in the IEEE format) and number of bytes (modulo `2^32`) of the uncompressed data.
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//!
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! The gzip header is purely a set of metadata, and doesn't have any impact on the decoding of the
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! compressed data other than the fact that `DEFLATE`-encoded data with a gzip-header is
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! checked using the CRC32 algorithm.
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! This library is based on the gzip header functionality in the
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! [flate2](https://crates.io/crates/flate2) crate.
[15](https://docs.rs#15)
[16](https://docs.rs#16)#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
[17](https://docs.rs#17)#![no_std]
[18](https://docs.rs#18)extern crate alloc;
[19](https://docs.rs#19)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[20](https://docs.rs#20)extern crate std;
[21](https://docs.rs#21)
[22](https://docs.rs#22)mod crc_reader;
[23](https://docs.rs#23)
[24](https://docs.rs#24)use alloc::borrow::Cow;
[25](https://docs.rs#25)use alloc::ffi::CString;
[26](https://docs.rs#26)use core::default::Default;
[27](https://docs.rs#27)use core::fmt;
[28](https://docs.rs#28)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[29](https://docs.rs#29)use std::io::Read;
[30](https://docs.rs#30)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[31](https://docs.rs#31)use std::{env, io, time};
[32](https://docs.rs#32)
[33](https://docs.rs#33)pub use crc_reader::Crc;
[34](https://docs.rs#34)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[35](https://docs.rs#35)pub use crc_reader::CrcReader;
[36](https://docs.rs#36)
[37](https://docs.rs#37)static FHCRC: u8 = 1 << 1;
[38](https://docs.rs#38)static FEXTRA: u8 = 1 << 2;
[39](https://docs.rs#39)static FNAME: u8 = 1 << 3;
[40](https://docs.rs#40)static FCOMMENT: u8 = 1 << 4;
[41](https://docs.rs#41)
[42](https://docs.rs#42)/// An enum describing the different OS types described in the gzip format.
[43](https://docs.rs#43)/// See http://www.gzip.org/format.txt (Additionally, the Apple(19) value is defined in the zlib
[44](https://docs.rs#44)/// library).
[45](https://docs.rs#45)#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[46](https://docs.rs#46)#[repr(u8)]
[47](https://docs.rs#47)pub enum FileSystemType {
[48](https://docs.rs#48)    ///MS-DOS/old FAT filesystem
[49](https://docs.rs#49)    Fat = 0,
[50](https://docs.rs#50)    Amiga = 1,
[51](https://docs.rs#51)    Vms = 2,
[52](https://docs.rs#52)    Unix = 3,
[53](https://docs.rs#53)    Vcms = 4,
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    AtariTos = 5,
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    Hpfs = 6,
[56](https://docs.rs#56)    /// Used for apple platforms. Newer encoders may use 19 instead for modern systems.
[57](https://docs.rs#57)    Macintosh = 7,
[58](https://docs.rs#58)    Zsystem = 8,
[59](https://docs.rs#59)    Cpm = 9,
[60](https://docs.rs#60)    /// This is used for Windows/NTFS in zlib newer than 1.2.11, but not in gzip due to following
[61](https://docs.rs#61)    /// updates to the ZIP format.
[62](https://docs.rs#62)    /// See https://github.com/madler/zlib/issues/235 and
[63](https://docs.rs#63)    /// https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/ce12c5cd00628bf8f680c98123a369974d32df15
[64](https://docs.rs#64)    Tops20OrNTFS = 10,
[65](https://docs.rs#65)    /// Used for Windows platforms for older zlib versions and other encoders.
[66](https://docs.rs#66)    NTFS = 11,
[67](https://docs.rs#67)    SmsQdos = 12,
[68](https://docs.rs#68)    Riscos = 13,
[69](https://docs.rs#69)    /// Newer fat filesystems (i.e FAT32).
[70](https://docs.rs#70)    Vfat = 14,
[71](https://docs.rs#71)    Mvs = 15,
[72](https://docs.rs#72)    Beos = 16,
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    TandemNsk = 17,
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    Theos = 18,
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    /// Modern apple platforms.
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    /// Defined in the zlib library (see zutil.h)
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    Apple = 19,
[78](https://docs.rs#78)    Unknown = 255,
[79](https://docs.rs#79)}
[80](https://docs.rs#80)
[81](https://docs.rs#81)impl FileSystemType {
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    /// Get the raw byte value of this `FileSystemType` variant.
[83](https://docs.rs#83)    pub const fn as_u8(&self) -> u8 {
[84](https://docs.rs#84)        *self as u8
[85](https://docs.rs#85)    }
[86](https://docs.rs#86)
[87](https://docs.rs#87)    /// Get the corresponding `ExtraFlags` value from a raw byte.
[88](https://docs.rs#88)    ///
[89](https://docs.rs#89)    /// Returns `FileSystemType::Unknown` (defined as 255 as that is the value used in the
[90](https://docs.rs#90)    /// specification for `Unknown`) if the value is not one of the currently known types
[91](https://docs.rs#91)    /// (Which currently means any value > 19).
[92](https://docs.rs#92)    pub fn from_u8(value: u8) -> FileSystemType {
[93](https://docs.rs#93)        use FileSystemType::*;
[94](https://docs.rs#94)        match value {
[95](https://docs.rs#95)            0 => Fat,
[96](https://docs.rs#96)            1 => Amiga,
[97](https://docs.rs#97)            2 => Vms,
[98](https://docs.rs#98)            3 => Unix,
[99](https://docs.rs#99)            4 => Vcms,
[100](https://docs.rs#100)            5 => AtariTos,
[101](https://docs.rs#101)            6 => Hpfs,
[102](https://docs.rs#102)            7 => Macintosh,
[103](https://docs.rs#103)            8 => Zsystem,
[104](https://docs.rs#104)            9 => Cpm,
[105](https://docs.rs#105)            10 => Tops20OrNTFS,
[106](https://docs.rs#106)            11 => NTFS,
[107](https://docs.rs#107)            12 => SmsQdos,
[108](https://docs.rs#108)            13 => Riscos,
[109](https://docs.rs#109)            14 => Vfat,
[110](https://docs.rs#110)            15 => Mvs,
[111](https://docs.rs#111)            16 => Beos,
[112](https://docs.rs#112)            17 => TandemNsk,
[113](https://docs.rs#113)            18 => Theos,
[114](https://docs.rs#114)            19 => Apple,
[115](https://docs.rs#115)            _ => Unknown,
[116](https://docs.rs#116)        }
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    }
[118](https://docs.rs#118)}

[149](https://docs.rs#149)
[150](https://docs.rs#150)/// Valid values for the extra flag in the gzip specification.
[151](https://docs.rs#151)///
[152](https://docs.rs#152)/// This is a field to be used by the compression methods. For deflate, which is the only
[153](https://docs.rs#153)/// specified compression method, this is a value indicating the level of compression of the
[154](https://docs.rs#154)/// contained compressed data. This value does not have to correspond to the actual compression
[155](https://docs.rs#155)/// level of the contained data, it's only a hint that the the encoder may set.
[156](https://docs.rs#156)#[derive(Default, Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[157](https://docs.rs#157)#[repr(u8)]
[158](https://docs.rs#158)pub enum ExtraFlags {
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    #[default]
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    Default = 0,
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    MaximumCompression = 2,
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    FastestCompression = 4,
[163](https://docs.rs#163)}
[164](https://docs.rs#164)
[165](https://docs.rs#165)impl ExtraFlags {
[166](https://docs.rs#166)    /// Get the corresponding `ExtraFlags` value from a raw byte.
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    ///
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    /// Returns `ExtraFlags::Default` (defined as 0 by the gzip specification) for values other than
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    /// 2 and 4.
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    pub fn from_u8(value: u8) -> ExtraFlags {
[171](https://docs.rs#171)        use ExtraFlags::*;
[172](https://docs.rs#172)        match value {
[173](https://docs.rs#173)            2 => MaximumCompression,
[174](https://docs.rs#174)            4 => FastestCompression,
[175](https://docs.rs#175)            _ => Default,
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        }
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    }
[178](https://docs.rs#178)
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    /// Get the raw byte value of this `ExtraFlags` variant.
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    pub const fn as_u8(&self) -> u8 {
[181](https://docs.rs#181)        *self as u8
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    }
[183](https://docs.rs#183)}
[184](https://docs.rs#184)
[185](https://docs.rs#185)impl fmt::Display for ExtraFlags {
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[187](https://docs.rs#187)        match *self {
[188](https://docs.rs#188)            ExtraFlags::Default => "No extra flags (Default) or unknown.",
[189](https://docs.rs#189)            ExtraFlags::MaximumCompression => "Maximum compression algorithm (DEFLATE).",
[190](https://docs.rs#190)            ExtraFlags::FastestCompression => "Fastest compression algorithm (DEFLATE)",
[191](https://docs.rs#191)        }
[192](https://docs.rs#192)        .fmt(f)
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    }
[194](https://docs.rs#194)}
[195](https://docs.rs#195)
[196](https://docs.rs#196)/// A builder structure to create a new gzip header.
[197](https://docs.rs#197)///
[198](https://docs.rs#198)/// This structure controls header configuration options such as the filename.
[199](https://docs.rs#199)#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
[200](https://docs.rs#200)pub struct GzBuilder {
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    extra: Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>,
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    filename: Option<CString>,
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    comment: Option<CString>,
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    // Whether this should be signed is a bit unclear, the gzip spec says mtime is in the unix
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    // time format, which is normally signed, however zlib seems to use an unsigned long for this
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    // field.
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    mtime: u32,
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    os: Option<FileSystemType>,
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    xfl: ExtraFlags,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)}
[211](https://docs.rs#211)
[212](https://docs.rs#212)impl GzBuilder {
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    /// Create a new blank builder with no header by default.
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    pub fn new() -> GzBuilder {
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        GzBuilder {
[216](https://docs.rs#216)            extra: None,
[217](https://docs.rs#217)            filename: None,
[218](https://docs.rs#218)            comment: None,
[219](https://docs.rs#219)            mtime: 0,
[220](https://docs.rs#220)            os: None,
[221](https://docs.rs#221)            xfl: ExtraFlags::Default,
[222](https://docs.rs#222)        }
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    }
[224](https://docs.rs#224)
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// Configure the `mtime` field in the gzip header.
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    pub fn mtime(mut self, mtime: u32) -> GzBuilder {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)        self.mtime = mtime;
[228](https://docs.rs#228)        self
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    }
[230](https://docs.rs#230)
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    /// Configure the `extra` field in the gzip header.
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    pub fn extra<T: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>>(mut self, extra: T) -> GzBuilder {
[233](https://docs.rs#233)        self.extra = Some(extra.into());
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        self
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    }
[236](https://docs.rs#236)
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    /// Configure the `filename` field in the gzip header.
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    ///
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    /// # Panics
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    /// Panics if the filename argument contains a byte with the value 0.
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    pub fn filename<T: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>>(mut self, filename: T) -> GzBuilder {
[242](https://docs.rs#242)        self.filename = Some(CString::new(filename).unwrap());
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        self
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    }
[245](https://docs.rs#245)
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    /// Configure the `comment` field in the gzip header.
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    ///
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    /// # Panics
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    /// Panics if the comment argument contains a byte with the value 0.
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    pub fn comment<T: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>>(mut self, comment: T) -> GzBuilder {
[251](https://docs.rs#251)        self.comment = Some(CString::new(comment).unwrap());
[252](https://docs.rs#252)        self
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    }
[254](https://docs.rs#254)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    /// Configure the `os` field in the gzip header.
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    ///
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    /// This is taken from `std::env::consts::OS` if not set explicitly.
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    pub fn os(mut self, os: FileSystemType) -> GzBuilder {
[259](https://docs.rs#259)        self.os = Some(os);
[260](https://docs.rs#260)        self
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    }
[262](https://docs.rs#262)
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    /// Configure the `xfl` field in the gzip header.
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    ///
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    /// The default is `ExtraFlags::Default` (meaning not set).
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    pub fn xfl(mut self, xfl: ExtraFlags) -> GzBuilder {
[267](https://docs.rs#267)        self.xfl = xfl;
[268](https://docs.rs#268)        self
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    }
[270](https://docs.rs#270)
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    /// Transforms this builder structure into a raw vector of bytes, setting the `XFL` field to the
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    /// value specified by `lvl`.
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    pub fn into_header_xfl(mut self, lvl: ExtraFlags) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
[274](https://docs.rs#274)        self.xfl = lvl;
[275](https://docs.rs#275)        self.into_header()
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    }
[277](https://docs.rs#277)
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    /// Transforms this builder structure into a raw vector of bytes.
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    pub fn into_header(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
[280](https://docs.rs#280)        self.into_header_inner(false)
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    }
[282](https://docs.rs#282)
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    /// Transforms this builder structure into a raw vector of bytes.
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    pub fn into_header_with_checksum(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
[285](https://docs.rs#285)        self.into_header_inner(true)
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    }
[287](https://docs.rs#287)
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    fn into_header_inner(self, use_crc: bool) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        let GzBuilder {
[290](https://docs.rs#290)            extra,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)            filename,
[292](https://docs.rs#292)            comment,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            mtime,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            os,
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            xfl,
[296](https://docs.rs#296)        } = self;
[297](https://docs.rs#297)        let os = match os {
[298](https://docs.rs#298)            Some(f) => f,
[299](https://docs.rs#299)            // Set the OS based on the system the binary is compiled for if not set,
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            // as this is a required field.
[301](https://docs.rs#301)            // These defaults are taken from what modern zlib uses, which are not the same as
[302](https://docs.rs#302)            // what's used in flate2.
[303](https://docs.rs#303)            None => {
[304](https://docs.rs#304)                #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[305](https://docs.rs#305)                match env::consts::OS {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)                    "linux" | "freebsd" | "dragonfly" | "netbsd" | "openbsd" | "solaris"
[307](https://docs.rs#307)                    | "bitrig" => FileSystemType::Unix,
[308](https://docs.rs#308)                    "macos" => FileSystemType::Apple,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)                    "win32" => FileSystemType::Tops20OrNTFS,
[310](https://docs.rs#310)                    _ => FileSystemType::Unknown,
[311](https://docs.rs#311)                }
[312](https://docs.rs#312)                #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[313](https://docs.rs#313)                FileSystemType::Unknown
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            }
[315](https://docs.rs#315)        };
[316](https://docs.rs#316)        let mut flg = 0;
[317](https://docs.rs#317)        if use_crc {
[318](https://docs.rs#318)            flg |= FHCRC;
[319](https://docs.rs#319)        };
[320](https://docs.rs#320)        let mut header = alloc::vec![0u8; 10];
[321](https://docs.rs#321)
[322](https://docs.rs#322)        if let Some(v) = extra {
[323](https://docs.rs#323)            flg |= FEXTRA;
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            header.push((v.len()/* >> 0*/) as u8);
[325](https://docs.rs#325)            header.push((v.len() >> 8) as u8);
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            header.extend(v);
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        }
[328](https://docs.rs#328)
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        if let Some(filename) = filename {
[330](https://docs.rs#330)            flg |= FNAME;
[331](https://docs.rs#331)            header.extend(filename.as_bytes_with_nul().iter().cloned());
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        }
[333](https://docs.rs#333)
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        if let Some(comment) = comment {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)            flg |= FCOMMENT;
[336](https://docs.rs#336)            header.extend(comment.as_bytes_with_nul().iter().cloned());
[337](https://docs.rs#337)        }
[338](https://docs.rs#338)
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        header[0] = 0x1f;
[340](https://docs.rs#340)        header[1] = 0x8b;
[341](https://docs.rs#341)        header[2] = 8;
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        header[3] = flg;
[343](https://docs.rs#343)        header[4] = mtime /*>> 0*/ as u8;
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        header[5] = (mtime >> 8) as u8;
[345](https://docs.rs#345)        header[6] = (mtime >> 16) as u8;
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        header[7] = (mtime >> 24) as u8;
[347](https://docs.rs#347)        header[8] = xfl.as_u8();
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        header[9] = os.as_u8();
[349](https://docs.rs#349)
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        if use_crc {
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            let mut crc = Crc::new();
[352](https://docs.rs#352)            crc.update(&header);
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            let checksum = crc.sum() as u16;
[354](https://docs.rs#354)            header.extend(&[checksum as u8, (checksum >> 8) as u8]);
[355](https://docs.rs#355)        }
[356](https://docs.rs#356)
[357](https://docs.rs#357)        header
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    }
[359](https://docs.rs#359)}
[360](https://docs.rs#360)
[361](https://docs.rs#361)/// A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.
[362](https://docs.rs#362)///
[363](https://docs.rs#363)/// The header can contain metadata about the file that was compressed, if
[364](https://docs.rs#364)/// present.
[365](https://docs.rs#365)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[366](https://docs.rs#366)pub struct GzHeader {

[370](https://docs.rs#370)    mtime: u32,
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    os: u8,
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    xfl: u8,
[373](https://docs.rs#373)}

[375](https://docs.rs#375)impl GzHeader {
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    /// Returns the `filename` field of this gzip header, if present.
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    ///
[378](https://docs.rs#378)    /// The `filename` field the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
[379](https://docs.rs#379)    /// encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    pub fn filename(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {

[382](https://docs.rs#382)    }

[387](https://docs.rs#387)    }
[388](https://docs.rs#388)
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    /// Returns the `comment` field of this gzip stream's header, if present.

[398](https://docs.rs#398)    ///
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// This gives the most recent modification time of the contained file, or alternatively
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// the timestamp of when the file was compressed if the data did not come from a file, or
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// a timestamp was not available when compressing. The time is specified the Unix format,
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    /// that is: seconds since 00:00:00 GMT, Jan. 1, 1970. (Not that this may cause problems for
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    /// MS-DOS and other systems that use local rather than Universal time.)
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    /// An `mtime` value of 0 means that the timestamp is not set.
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    pub const fn mtime(&self) -> u32 {
[406](https://docs.rs#406)        self.mtime
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    }
[408](https://docs.rs#408)
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    /// Returns the `mtime` field of this gzip header as a `SystemTime` if present.
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    ///
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    /// Returns `None` if the `mtime` is not set, i.e 0.
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    /// See [`mtime`](#method.mtime) for more detail.
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    pub fn mtime_as_datetime(&self) -> Option<time::SystemTime> {
[415](https://docs.rs#415)        if self.mtime == 0 {
[416](https://docs.rs#416)            None
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        } else {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)            let duration = time::Duration::new(u64::from(self.mtime), 0);
[419](https://docs.rs#419)            let datetime = time::UNIX_EPOCH + duration;
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            Some(datetime)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        }
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    }

[477](https://docs.rs#477)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[478](https://docs.rs#478)fn bad_header() -> io::Error {
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "invalid gzip header")
[480](https://docs.rs#480)}
[481](https://docs.rs#481)
[482](https://docs.rs#482)/// Try to read a little-endian u16 from the provided reader.
[483](https://docs.rs#483)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[484](https://docs.rs#484)fn read_le_u16<R: Read>(r: &mut R) -> io::Result<u16> {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    let mut b = [0; 2];
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    r.read_exact(&mut b)?;
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    Ok((b[0] as u16) | ((b[1] as u16) << 8))
[488](https://docs.rs#488)}
[489](https://docs.rs#489)
[490](https://docs.rs#490)/// Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.
[491](https://docs.rs#491)///
[492](https://docs.rs#492)/// Returns a `GzHeader` with the fields filled out if sucessful, or an `io::Error` with
[493](https://docs.rs#493)/// `ErrorKind::InvalidInput` if decoding of the header.
[494](https://docs.rs#494)///
[495](https://docs.rs#495)/// Note that a gzip steam can contain multiple "members". Each member contains a header,
[496](https://docs.rs#496)/// followed by compressed data and finally a checksum and byte count.
[497](https://docs.rs#497)/// This method will only read the header for the "member" at the start of the stream.
[498](https://docs.rs#498)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[499](https://docs.rs#499)pub fn read_gz_header<R: Read>(r: &mut R) -> io::Result<GzHeader> {
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    let mut crc_reader = CrcReader::new(r);
[501](https://docs.rs#501)    let mut header = [0; 10];
[502](https://docs.rs#502)    crc_reader.read_exact(&mut header)?;
[503](https://docs.rs#503)
[504](https://docs.rs#504)    // `ID1` and `ID2` are fixed values to identify a gzip file.
[505](https://docs.rs#505)    let id1 = header[0];
[506](https://docs.rs#506)    let id2 = header[1];
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    if id1 != 0x1f || id2 != 0x8b {
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        return Err(bad_header());
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    }
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    // `CM` describes the compression method. Currently only method 8 (DEFLATE) is specified.
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    // by the gzip format.
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    let cm = header[2];
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    if cm != 8 {
[514](https://docs.rs#514)        return Err(bad_header());
[515](https://docs.rs#515)    }
[516](https://docs.rs#516)
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    // `FLG` the bits in this field indicates whether the `FTEXT`, `FHCRC`, `FEXTRA`, `FNAME` and
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    // `FCOMMENT` fields are present in the header.
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    let flg = header[3];
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    let mtime = (header[4] as u32/* << 0*/)
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        | ((header[5] as u32) << 8)
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        | ((header[6] as u32) << 16)
[523](https://docs.rs#523)        | ((header[7] as u32) << 24);
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    // `XFL` describes the compression level used by the encoder. (May not actually
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    // match what the encoder used and has no impact on decompression.)
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    let xfl = header[8];
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    // `os` describes what type of operating system/file system the file was created on.
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    let os = header[9];
[529](https://docs.rs#529)
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    let extra = if flg & FEXTRA != 0 {
[531](https://docs.rs#531)        // Length of the FEXTRA field.
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        let xlen = read_le_u16(&mut crc_reader)?;
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        let mut extra = alloc::vec![0; xlen as usize];
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        crc_reader.read_exact(&mut extra)?;
[535](https://docs.rs#535)        Some(extra)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    } else {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        None
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    };
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    let filename = if flg & FNAME != 0 {
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        // wow this is slow
[541](https://docs.rs#541)        let mut b = alloc::vec::Vec::new();
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        for byte in crc_reader.by_ref().bytes() {
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            let byte = byte?;
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            if byte == 0 {
[545](https://docs.rs#545)                break;
[546](https://docs.rs#546)            }
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            b.push(byte);
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        }
[549](https://docs.rs#549)        Some(b)
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    } else {
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        None
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    };
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    let comment = if flg & FCOMMENT != 0 {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        // wow this is slow
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        let mut b = alloc::vec::Vec::new();
[556](https://docs.rs#556)        for byte in crc_reader.by_ref().bytes() {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)            let byte = byte?;
[558](https://docs.rs#558)            if byte == 0 {
[559](https://docs.rs#559)                break;
[560](https://docs.rs#560)            }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)            b.push(byte);
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        }
[563](https://docs.rs#563)        Some(b)
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    } else {
[565](https://docs.rs#565)        None
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    };
[567](https://docs.rs#567)
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    // If the `FHCRC` flag is set, the header contains a two-byte CRC16 checksum of the header bytes
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    // that needs to be validated.
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    if flg & FHCRC != 0 {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        let calced_crc = crc_reader.crc().sum() as u16;
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        let stored_crc = read_le_u16(&mut crc_reader)?;
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        if calced_crc != stored_crc {
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            return Err(corrupt());
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        }
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    }
[577](https://docs.rs#577)
[578](https://docs.rs#578)    Ok(GzHeader {
[579](https://docs.rs#579)        extra,
[580](https://docs.rs#580)        filename,
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        comment,
[582](https://docs.rs#582)        mtime,
[583](https://docs.rs#583)        os,
[584](https://docs.rs#584)        xfl,
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    })
[586](https://docs.rs#586)}
[587](https://docs.rs#587)
[588](https://docs.rs#588)#[cfg(test)]
[589](https://docs.rs#589)mod tests {
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    extern crate std;
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    use super::*;
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    use std::io::Cursor;
[593](https://docs.rs#593)
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    fn roundtrip_inner(use_crc: bool) {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        const COMMENT: &[u8] = b"Comment";
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        const FILENAME: &[u8] = b"Filename";
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        const MTIME: u32 = 12345;
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        const OS: FileSystemType = FileSystemType::NTFS;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        const XFL: ExtraFlags = ExtraFlags::FastestCompression;
[600](https://docs.rs#600)
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        let header = GzBuilder::new()
[602](https://docs.rs#602)            .comment(COMMENT)
[603](https://docs.rs#603)            .filename(FILENAME)
[604](https://docs.rs#604)            .mtime(MTIME)
[605](https://docs.rs#605)            .os(OS)
[606](https://docs.rs#606)            .xfl(ExtraFlags::FastestCompression)
[607](https://docs.rs#607)            .into_header_inner(use_crc);
[608](https://docs.rs#608)
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        let mut reader = Cursor::new(header.clone());
[610](https://docs.rs#610)
[611](https://docs.rs#611)        let header_read = read_gz_header(&mut reader).unwrap();
[612](https://docs.rs#612)
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        assert_eq!(header_read.comment().unwrap(), COMMENT);
[614](https://docs.rs#614)        assert_eq!(header_read.filename().unwrap(), FILENAME);
[615](https://docs.rs#615)        assert_eq!(header_read.mtime(), MTIME);
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        assert_eq!(header_read.os(), OS.as_u8());
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        assert_eq!(header_read.xfl(), XFL.as_u8());
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    }
[619](https://docs.rs#619)
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    #[test]
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    fn roundtrip() {
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        roundtrip_inner(false);
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    }
[624](https://docs.rs#624)
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    #[test]
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    fn roundtrip_with_crc() {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        roundtrip_inner(true);
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    #[test]
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    fn filesystem_enum() {
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        for n in 0..20 {
[633](https://docs.rs#633)            assert_eq!(n, FileSystemType::from_u8(n).as_u8());
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        for n in 20..(u8::MAX as u16) + 1 {
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            assert_eq!(FileSystemType::from_u8(n as u8), FileSystemType::Unknown);
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        }
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    }

# GzBuilder in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gzip-header/1.1.0/gzip_header/struct.GzBuilder.html

`pub struct GzBuilder { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A builder structure to create a new gzip header.

This structure controls header configuration options such as the filename.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# GzHeader in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/gzip-header/1.1.0/gzip_header/struct.GzHeader.html

`pub struct GzHeader { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.

The header can contain metadata about the file that was compressed, if present.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Returns the `filename` field of this gzip header, if present.

The `filename` field the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.

Returns the `comment` field of this gzip stream’s header, if present.

The `comment` field in the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.

Returns the `mtime` field of this gzip header.

This gives the most recent modification time of the contained file, or alternatively
the timestamp of when the file was compressed if the data did not come from a file, or
a timestamp was not available when compressing. The time is specified the Unix format,
that is: seconds since 00:00:00 GMT, Jan. 1, 1970. (Not that this may cause problems for
MS-DOS and other systems that use local rather than Universal time.)
An `mtime` value of 0 means that the timestamp is not set.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Crudely display the contents of the header

Note that filename/commend are required to be ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1) encoded by the spec, however to avoid dragging in dependencies we simply interpret them as UTF-8. This may result in garbled output if the names contain special characters.
