[275](https://docs.rs#275)        self.into_header()
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    }
[277](https://docs.rs#277)
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    /// Transforms this builder structure into a raw vector of bytes.
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    pub fn into_header(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
[280](https://docs.rs#280)        self.into_header_inner(false)
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    }
[282](https://docs.rs#282)
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    /// Transforms this builder structure into a raw vector of bytes.
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    pub fn into_header_with_checksum(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
[285](https://docs.rs#285)        self.into_header_inner(true)
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    }
[287](https://docs.rs#287)
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    fn into_header_inner(self, use_crc: bool) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        let GzBuilder {
[290](https://docs.rs#290)            extra,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)            filename,
[292](https://docs.rs#292)            comment,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            mtime,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            os,
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            xfl,
[296](https://docs.rs#296)        } = self;
[297](https://docs.rs#297)        let os = match os {
[298](https://docs.rs#298)            Some(f) => f,
[299](https://docs.rs#299)            // Set the OS based on the system the binary is compiled for if not set,
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            // as this is a required field.
[301](https://docs.rs#301)            // These defaults are taken from what modern zlib uses, which are not the same as
[302](https://docs.rs#302)            // what's used in flate2.
[303](https://docs.rs#303)            None => {
[304](https://docs.rs#304)                #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[305](https://docs.rs#305)                match env::consts::OS {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)                    "linux" | "freebsd" | "dragonfly" | "netbsd" | "openbsd" | "solaris"
[307](https://docs.rs#307)                    | "bitrig" => FileSystemType::Unix,
[308](https://docs.rs#308)                    "macos" => FileSystemType::Apple,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)                    "win32" => FileSystemType::Tops20OrNTFS,
[310](https://docs.rs#310)                    _ => FileSystemType::Unknown,
[311](https://docs.rs#311)                }
[312](https://docs.rs#312)                #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[313](https://docs.rs#313)                FileSystemType::Unknown
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            }
[315](https://docs.rs#315)        };
[316](https://docs.rs#316)        let mut flg = 0;
[317](https://docs.rs#317)        if use_crc {
[318](https://docs.rs#318)            flg |= FHCRC;
[319](https://docs.rs#319)        };
[320](https://docs.rs#320)        let mut header = alloc::vec![0u8; 10];
[321](https://docs.rs#321)
[322](https://docs.rs#322)        if let Some(v) = extra {
[323](https://docs.rs#323)            flg |= FEXTRA;
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            header.push((v.len()/* >> 0*/) as u8);
[325](https://docs.rs#325)            header.push((v.len() >> 8) as u8);
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            header.extend(v);
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        }
[328](https://docs.rs#328)
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        if let Some(filename) = filename {
[330](https://docs.rs#330)            flg |= FNAME;
[331](https://docs.rs#331)            header.extend(filename.as_bytes_with_nul().iter().cloned());
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        }
[333](https://docs.rs#333)
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        if let Some(comment) = comment {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)            flg |= FCOMMENT;
[336](https://docs.rs#336)            header.extend(comment.as_bytes_with_nul().iter().cloned());
[337](https://docs.rs#337)        }
[338](https://docs.rs#338)
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        header[0] = 0x1f;
[340](https://docs.rs#340)        header[1] = 0x8b;
[341](https://docs.rs#341)        header[2] = 8;
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        header[3] = flg;
[343](https://docs.rs#343)        header[4] = mtime /*>> 0*/ as u8;
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        header[5] = (mtime >> 8) as u8;
[345](https://docs.rs#345)        header[6] = (mtime >> 16) as u8;
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        header[7] = (mtime >> 24) as u8;
[347](https://docs.rs#347)        header[8] = xfl.as_u8();
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        header[9] = os.as_u8();
[349](https://docs.rs#349)
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        if use_crc {
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            let mut crc = Crc::new();
[352](https://docs.rs#352)            crc.update(&header);
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            let checksum = crc.sum() as u16;
[354](https://docs.rs#354)            header.extend(&[checksum as u8, (checksum >> 8) as u8]);
[355](https://docs.rs#355)        }
[356](https://docs.rs#356)
[357](https://docs.rs#357)        header
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    }
[359](https://docs.rs#359)}
[360](https://docs.rs#360)
[361](https://docs.rs#361)/// A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.
[362](https://docs.rs#362)///
[363](https://docs.rs#363)/// The header can contain metadata about the file that was compressed, if
[364](https://docs.rs#364)/// present.
[365](https://docs.rs#365)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[366](https://docs.rs#366)pub struct GzHeader {
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    extra: Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>,
[368](https://docs.rs#368)    filename: Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>,
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    comment: Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>,
[370](https://docs.rs#370)    mtime: u32,
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    os: u8,
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    xfl: u8,
[373](https://docs.rs#373)}
[374](https://docs.rs#374)
[375](https://docs.rs#375)impl GzHeader {
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    /// Returns the `filename` field of this gzip header, if present.
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    ///
[378](https://docs.rs#378)    /// The `filename` field the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
[379](https://docs.rs#379)    /// encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    pub fn filename(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {
[381](https://docs.rs#381)        self.filename.as_ref().map(|s| &s[..])
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    }
[383](https://docs.rs#383)
[384](https://docs.rs#384)    /// Returns the `extra` field of this gzip header, if present.
[385](https://docs.rs#385)    pub fn extra(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        self.extra.as_ref().map(|s| &s[..])
[387](https://docs.rs#387)    }
[388](https://docs.rs#388)
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    /// Returns the `comment` field of this gzip stream's header, if present.
[390](https://docs.rs#390)    ///
[391](https://docs.rs#391)    /// The `comment` field in the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
[392](https://docs.rs#392)    /// encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.
[393](https://docs.rs#393)    pub fn comment(&self) -> Option<&[u8]> {
[394](https://docs.rs#394)        self.comment.as_ref().map(|s| &s[..])
[395](https://docs.rs#395)    }
[396](https://docs.rs#396)
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    /// Returns the `mtime` field of this gzip header.
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    ///
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// This gives the most recent modification time of the contained file, or alternatively
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// the timestamp of when the file was compressed if the data did not come from a file, or
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// a timestamp was not available when compressing. The time is specified the Unix format,
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    /// that is: seconds since 00:00:00 GMT, Jan. 1, 1970. (Not that this may cause problems for
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    /// MS-DOS and other systems that use local rather than Universal time.)
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    /// An `mtime` value of 0 means that the timestamp is not set.
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    pub const fn mtime(&self) -> u32 {
[406](https://docs.rs#406)        self.mtime
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    }
[408](https://docs.rs#408)
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    /// Returns the `mtime` field of this gzip header as a `SystemTime` if present.
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    ///
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    /// Returns `None` if the `mtime` is not set, i.e 0.
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    /// See [`mtime`](#method.mtime) for more detail.
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    pub fn mtime_as_datetime(&self) -> Option<time::SystemTime> {
[415](https://docs.rs#415)        if self.mtime == 0 {
[416](https://docs.rs#416)            None
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        } else {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)            let duration = time::Duration::new(u64::from(self.mtime), 0);
[419](https://docs.rs#419)            let datetime = time::UNIX_EPOCH + duration;
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            Some(datetime)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        }
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    }
[423](https://docs.rs#423)
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    /// Returns the `os` field of this gzip stream's header.
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    pub const fn os(&self) -> u8 {
[426](https://docs.rs#426)        self.os
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    }
[428](https://docs.rs#428)
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    /// Returns the `xfl` field of this gzip stream's header.
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    pub const fn xfl(&self) -> u8 {
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        self.xfl
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    }
[433](https://docs.rs#433)}
[434](https://docs.rs#434)
[435](https://docs.rs#435)#[inline]
[436](https://docs.rs#436)fn into_string<'a>(data: Option<&'a [u8]>) -> alloc::borrow::Cow<'a, str> {
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    data.map_or_else(
[438](https://docs.rs#438)        || Cow::Borrowed("(Not set)"),
[439](https://docs.rs#439)        |d| alloc::string::String::from_utf8_lossy(d),
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    )
[441](https://docs.rs#441)}
[442](https://docs.rs#442)
[443](https://docs.rs#443)impl fmt::Display for GzHeader {
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    /// Crudely display the contents of the header
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    ///
[446](https://docs.rs#446)    /// Note that filename/commend are required to be ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1) encoded by the spec,
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    /// however to avoid dragging in dependencies we simply interpret them as UTF-8.
[448](https://docs.rs#448)    /// This may result in garbled output if the names contain special characters.
[449](https://docs.rs#449)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
[450](https://docs.rs#450)        write!(
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            f,
[452](https://docs.rs#452)            "Filename: {}\n\
[453](https://docs.rs#453)             Comment: {}\n\
[454](https://docs.rs#454)             Extra: {:?}\n\
[455](https://docs.rs#455)             mtime: {}\n\
[456](https://docs.rs#456)             os: {}\n\
[457](https://docs.rs#457)             xfl: {}",
[458](https://docs.rs#458)            into_string(self.filename()),
[459](https://docs.rs#459)            into_string(self.comment()),
[460](https://docs.rs#460)            // We display extra as raw bytes for now.
[461](https://docs.rs#461)            self.extra,
[462](https://docs.rs#462)            self.mtime,
[463](https://docs.rs#463)            FileSystemType::from_u8(self.os),
[464](https://docs.rs#464)            ExtraFlags::Default, //ExtraFlags::from_u8(self.xfl),
[465](https://docs.rs#465)        )
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    }
[467](https://docs.rs#467)}
[468](https://docs.rs#468)
[469](https://docs.rs#469)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[470](https://docs.rs#470)fn corrupt() -> io::Error {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)    io::Error::new(
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput,
[473](https://docs.rs#473)        "corrupt gzip stream does not have a matching header checksum",
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    )
[475](https://docs.rs#475)}
[476](https://docs.rs#476)
[477](https://docs.rs#477)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[478](https://docs.rs#478)fn bad_header() -> io::Error {
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "invalid gzip header")
[480](https://docs.rs#480)}
[481](https://docs.rs#481)
[482](https://docs.rs#482)/// Try to read a little-endian u16 from the provided reader.
[483](https://docs.rs#483)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[484](https://docs.rs#484)fn read_le_u16<R: Read>(r: &mut R) -> io::Result<u16> {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    let mut b = [0; 2];
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    r.read_exact(&mut b)?;
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    Ok((b[0] as u16) | ((b[1] as u16) << 8))
[488](https://docs.rs#488)}
[489](https://docs.rs#489)
[490](https://docs.rs#490)/// Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.
[491](https://docs.rs#491)///
[492](https://docs.rs#492)/// Returns a `GzHeader` with the fields filled out if sucessful, or an `io::Error` with
[493](https://docs.rs#493)/// `ErrorKind::InvalidInput` if decoding of the header.
[494](https://docs.rs#494)///
[495](https://docs.rs#495)/// Note that a gzip steam can contain multiple "members". Each member contains a header,
[496](https://docs.rs#496)/// followed by compressed data and finally a checksum and byte count.
[497](https://docs.rs#497)/// This method will only read the header for the "member" at the start of the stream.
[498](https://docs.rs#498)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[499](https://docs.rs#499)pub fn read_gz_header<R: Read>(r: &mut R) -> io::Result<GzHeader> {
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    let mut crc_reader = CrcReader::new(r);
[501](https://docs.rs#501)    let mut header = [0; 10];
[502](https://docs.rs#502)    crc_reader.read_exact(&mut header)?;
[503](https://docs.rs#503)
[504](https://docs.rs#504)    // `ID1` and `ID2` are fixed values to identify a gzip file.
[505](https://docs.rs#505)    let id1 = header[0];
[506](https://docs.rs#506)    let id2 = header[1];
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    if id1 != 0x1f || id2 != 0x8b {
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        return Err(bad_header());
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    }
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    // `CM` describes the compression method. Currently only method 8 (DEFLATE) is specified.
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    // by the gzip format.
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    let cm = header[2];
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    if cm != 8 {
[514](https://docs.rs#514)        return Err(bad_header());
[515](https://docs.rs#515)    }
[516](https://docs.rs#516)
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    // `FLG` the bits in this field indicates whether the `FTEXT`, `FHCRC`, `FEXTRA`, `FNAME` and
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    // `FCOMMENT` fields are present in the header.
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    let flg = header[3];
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    let mtime = (header[4] as u32/* << 0*/)
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        | ((header[5] as u32) << 8)
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        | ((header[6] as u32) << 16)
[523](https://docs.rs#523)        | ((header[7] as u32) << 24);
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    // `XFL` describes the compression level used by the encoder. (May not actually
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    // match what the encoder used and has no impact on decompression.)
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    let xfl = header[8];
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    // `os` describes what type of operating system/file system the file was created on.
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    let os = header[9];
[529](https://docs.rs#529)
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    let extra = if flg & FEXTRA != 0 {
[531](https://docs.rs#531)        // Length of the FEXTRA field.
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        let xlen = read_le_u16(&mut crc_reader)?;
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        let mut extra = alloc::vec![0; xlen as usize];
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        crc_reader.read_exact(&mut extra)?;
[535](https://docs.rs#535)        Some(extra)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    } else {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        None
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    };
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    let filename = if flg & FNAME != 0 {
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        // wow this is slow
[541](https://docs.rs#541)        let mut b = alloc::vec::Vec::new();
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        for byte in crc_reader.by_ref().bytes() {
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            let byte = byte?;
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            if byte == 0 {
[545](https://docs.rs#545)                break;
[546](https://docs.rs#546)            }
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            b.push(byte);
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        }
[549](https://docs.rs#549)        Some(b)
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    } else {
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        None
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    };
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    let comment = if flg & FCOMMENT != 0 {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        // wow this is slow
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        let mut b = alloc::vec::Vec::new();
[556](https://docs.rs#556)        for byte in crc_reader.by_ref().bytes() {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)            let byte = byte?;
[558](https://docs.rs#558)            if byte == 0 {
[559](https://docs.rs#559)                break;
[560](https://docs.rs#560)            }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)            b.push(byte);
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        }
[563](https://docs.rs#563)        Some(b)
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    } else {
[565](https://docs.rs#565)        None
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    };
[567](https://docs.rs#567)
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    // If the `FHCRC` flag is set, the header contains a two-byte CRC16 checksum of the header bytes
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    // that needs to be validated.
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    if flg & FHCRC != 0 {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        let calced_crc = crc_reader.crc().sum() as u16;
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        let stored_crc = read_le_u16(&mut crc_reader)?;
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        if calced_crc != stored_crc {
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            return Err(corrupt());
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        }
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    }
[577](https://docs.rs#577)
[578](https://docs.rs#578)    Ok(GzHeader {
[579](https://docs.rs#579)        extra,
[580](https://docs.rs#580)        filename,
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        comment,
[582](https://docs.rs#582)        mtime,
[583](https://docs.rs#583)        os,
[584](https://docs.rs#584)        xfl,
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    })
[586](https://docs.rs#586)}
[587](https://docs.rs#587)
[588](https://docs.rs#588)#[cfg(test)]
[589](https://docs.rs#589)mod tests {
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    extern crate std;
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    use super::*;
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    use std::io::Cursor;
[593](https://docs.rs#593)
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    fn roundtrip_inner(use_crc: bool) {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        const COMMENT: &[u8] = b"Comment";
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        const FILENAME: &[u8] = b"Filename";
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        const MTIME: u32 = 12345;
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        const OS: FileSystemType = FileSystemType::NTFS;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        const XFL: ExtraFlags = ExtraFlags::FastestCompression;
[600](https://docs.rs#600)
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        let header = GzBuilder::new()
[602](https://docs.rs#602)            .comment(COMMENT)
[603](https://docs.rs#603)            .filename(FILENAME)
[604](https://docs.rs#604)            .mtime(MTIME)
[605](https://docs.rs#605)            .os(OS)
[606](https://docs.rs#606)            .xfl(ExtraFlags::FastestCompression)
[607](https://docs.rs#607)            .into_header_inner(use_crc);
[608](https://docs.rs#608)
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        let mut reader = Cursor::new(header.clone());
[610](https://docs.rs#610)
[611](https://docs.rs#611)        let header_read = read_gz_header(&mut reader).unwrap();
[612](https://docs.rs#612)
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        assert_eq!(header_read.comment().unwrap(), COMMENT);
[614](https://docs.rs#614)        assert_eq!(header_read.filename().unwrap(), FILENAME);
[615](https://docs.rs#615)        assert_eq!(header_read.mtime(), MTIME);
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        assert_eq!(header_read.os(), OS.as_u8());
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        assert_eq!(header_read.xfl(), XFL.as_u8());
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    }
[619](https://docs.rs#619)
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    #[test]
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    fn roundtrip() {
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        roundtrip_inner(false);
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    }
[624](https://docs.rs#624)
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    #[test]
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    fn roundtrip_with_crc() {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        roundtrip_inner(true);
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    #[test]
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    fn filesystem_enum() {
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        for n in 0..20 {
[633](https://docs.rs#633)            assert_eq!(n, FileSystemType::from_u8(n).as_u8());
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)

[637](https://docs.rs#637)            assert_eq!(FileSystemType::from_u8(n as u8), FileSystemType::Unknown);
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        }
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    }

# GzHeader in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/gzip_header/struct.GzHeader.html

`pub struct GzHeader { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.

The header can contain metadata about the file that was compressed, if present.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Returns the `filename` field of this gzip header, if present.

The `filename` field the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.

Returns the `comment` field of this gzip stream’s header, if present.

The `comment` field in the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.

Returns the `mtime` field of this gzip header.

This gives the most recent modification time of the contained file, or alternatively
the timestamp of when the file was compressed if the data did not come from a file, or
a timestamp was not available when compressing. The time is specified the Unix format,
that is: seconds since 00:00:00 GMT, Jan. 1, 1970. (Not that this may cause problems for
MS-DOS and other systems that use local rather than Universal time.)
An `mtime` value of 0 means that the timestamp is not set.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Crudely display the contents of the header

Note that filename/commend are required to be ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1) encoded by the spec, however to avoid dragging in dependencies we simply interpret them as UTF-8. This may result in garbled output if the names contain special characters.

# ExtraFlags in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/gzip_header/enum.ExtraFlags.html

```
#[repr(u8)]pub enum ExtraFlags {
    Default = 0,
    MaximumCompression = 2,
    FastestCompression = 4,
}
```
## Expand description

Valid values for the extra flag in the gzip specification.

This is a field to be used by the compression methods. For deflate, which is the only specified compression method, this is a value indicating the level of compression of the contained compressed data. This value does not have to correspond to the actual compression level of the contained data, it’s only a hint that the the encoder may set.

# FileSystemType in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/gzip_header/enum.FileSystemType.html

```
#[repr(u8)]pub enum FileSystemType {
```
## Show 21 variants

    Fat = 0,
    Amiga = 1,
    Vms = 2,
    Unix = 3,
    Vcms = 4,
    AtariTos = 5,
    Hpfs = 6,
    Macintosh = 7,
    Zsystem = 8,
    Cpm = 9,
    Tops20OrNTFS = 10,
    NTFS = 11,
    SmsQdos = 12,
    Riscos = 13,
    Vfat = 14,
    Mvs = 15,
    Beos = 16,
    TandemNsk = 17,
    Theos = 18,
    Apple = 19,
    Unknown = 255,
}## Expand description

An enum describing the different OS types described in the gzip format. See http://www.gzip.org/format.txt (Additionally, the Apple(19) value is defined in the zlib library).

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Fat)

### Fat = 0

MS-DOS/old FAT filesystem

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Amiga)

### Amiga = 1

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Vms)

### Vms = 2

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unix)

### Unix = 3

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Vcms)

### Vcms = 4

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AtariTos)

### AtariTos = 5

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hpfs)

### Hpfs = 6

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Macintosh)

### Macintosh = 7

Used for apple platforms. Newer encoders may use 19 instead for modern systems.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Zsystem)

### Zsystem = 8

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Cpm)

### Cpm = 9

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Tops20OrNTFS)

### Tops20OrNTFS = 10

This is used for Windows/NTFS in zlib newer than 1.2.11, but not in gzip due to following updates to the ZIP format. See https://github.com/madler/zlib/issues/235 and https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/ce12c5cd00628bf8f680c98123a369974d32df15

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NTFS)

### NTFS = 11

Used for Windows platforms for older zlib versions and other encoders.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SmsQdos)

### SmsQdos = 12

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Riscos)

### Riscos = 13

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Vfat)

### Vfat = 14

Newer fat filesystems (i.e FAT32).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Mvs)

### Mvs = 15

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Beos)

### Beos = 16

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TandemNsk)

### TandemNsk = 17

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Theos)

### Theos = 18

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Apple)

Modern apple platforms. Defined in the zlib library (see zutil.h)

Returns `FileSystemType::Unknown` (defined as 255 as that is the value used in the
specification for `Unknown`) if the value is not one of the currently known types

# read_gz_header in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/gzip_header/fn.read_gz_header.html

## Expand description

Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.

Returns a `GzHeader` with the fields filled out if sucessful, or an `io::Error` with
`ErrorKind::InvalidInput` if decoding of the header.

Note that a gzip steam can contain multiple “members”. Each member contains a header, followed by compressed data and finally a checksum and byte count. This method will only read the header for the “member” at the start of the stream.

---

# gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/gzip_header/index.html

## Expand description

A library to decode and encode headers for the
[gzip format](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-gzip.html).
The library also contains a reader absctraction over a CRC checksum hasher.

A file in the gzip format contains a gzip header, a number of compressed data blocks in the
[DEFLATE](http://www.gzip.org/zlib/rfc-deflate.html) format, and ends with the CRC32-checksum
(in the IEEE format) and number of bytes (modulo `2^32`) of the uncompressed data.

The gzip header is purely a set of metadata, and doesn’t have any impact on the decoding of the
compressed data other than the fact that `DEFLATE`-encoded data with a gzip-header is
checked using the CRC32 algorithm.

This library is based on the gzip header functionality in the
[flate2](https://crates.io/crates/flate2) crate.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Crc](https://docs.rs/struct.Crc.html)
- A wrapper struct containing a CRC checksum in the format used by gzip and the amount of bytes input to it mod 2^32.
- [CrcReader](https://docs.rs/struct.CrcReader.html)
- A reader that updates the checksum and counter of a `Crc`struct when reading from the wrapped reader.
- [GzBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.GzBuilder.html)
- A builder structure to create a new gzip header.
- [GzHeader](https://docs.rs/struct.GzHeader.html)
- A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Extra](https://docs.rs/enum.ExtraFlags.html)- Flags
- Valid values for the extra flag in the gzip specification.
- [File](https://docs.rs/enum.FileSystemType.html)- System - Type
- An enum describing the different OS types described in the gzip format. See http://www.gzip.org/format.txt (Additionally, the Apple(19) value is defined in the zlib library).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [read_](https://docs.rs/fn.read_gz_header.html)- gz_ - header
- Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.

[47](https://docs.rs#47)pub enum FileSystemType {
[48](https://docs.rs#48)    ///MS-DOS/old FAT filesystem
[49](https://docs.rs#49)    Fat = 0,
[50](https://docs.rs#50)    Amiga = 1,
[51](https://docs.rs#51)    Vms = 2,
[52](https://docs.rs#52)    Unix = 3,
[53](https://docs.rs#53)    Vcms = 4,
[54](https://docs.rs#54)    AtariTos = 5,
[55](https://docs.rs#55)    Hpfs = 6,
[56](https://docs.rs#56)    /// Used for apple platforms. Newer encoders may use 19 instead for modern systems.
[57](https://docs.rs#57)    Macintosh = 7,
[58](https://docs.rs#58)    Zsystem = 8,
[59](https://docs.rs#59)    Cpm = 9,
[60](https://docs.rs#60)    /// This is used for Windows/NTFS in zlib newer than 1.2.11, but not in gzip due to following
[61](https://docs.rs#61)    /// updates to the ZIP format.
[62](https://docs.rs#62)    /// See https://github.com/madler/zlib/issues/235 and
[63](https://docs.rs#63)    /// https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/ce12c5cd00628bf8f680c98123a369974d32df15
[64](https://docs.rs#64)    Tops20OrNTFS = 10,
[65](https://docs.rs#65)    /// Used for Windows platforms for older zlib versions and other encoders.
[66](https://docs.rs#66)    NTFS = 11,
[67](https://docs.rs#67)    SmsQdos = 12,
[68](https://docs.rs#68)    Riscos = 13,
[69](https://docs.rs#69)    /// Newer fat filesystems (i.e FAT32).
[70](https://docs.rs#70)    Vfat = 14,
[71](https://docs.rs#71)    Mvs = 15,
[72](https://docs.rs#72)    Beos = 16,
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    TandemNsk = 17,
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    Theos = 18,
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    /// Modern apple platforms.
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    /// Defined in the zlib library (see zutil.h)
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    Apple = 19,

[150](https://docs.rs#150)/// Valid values for the extra flag in the gzip specification.
[151](https://docs.rs#151)///
[152](https://docs.rs#152)/// This is a field to be used by the compression methods. For deflate, which is the only
[153](https://docs.rs#153)/// specified compression method, this is a value indicating the level of compression of the
[154](https://docs.rs#154)/// contained compressed data. This value does not have to correspond to the actual compression
[155](https://docs.rs#155)/// level of the contained data, it's only a hint that the the encoder may set.
[156](https://docs.rs#156)#[derive(Default, Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[157](https://docs.rs#157)#[repr(u8)]
[158](https://docs.rs#158)pub enum ExtraFlags {
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    #[default]
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    Default = 0,
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    MaximumCompression = 2,
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    FastestCompression = 4,
[163](https://docs.rs#163)}
[164](https://docs.rs#164)

[171](https://docs.rs#171)        use ExtraFlags::*;
[172](https://docs.rs#172)        match value {
[173](https://docs.rs#173)            2 => MaximumCompression,
[174](https://docs.rs#174)            4 => FastestCompression,
[175](https://docs.rs#175)            _ => Default,
[176](https://docs.rs#176)        }
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    }

[196](https://docs.rs#196)/// A builder structure to create a new gzip header.
[197](https://docs.rs#197)///
[198](https://docs.rs#198)/// This structure controls header configuration options such as the filename.
[199](https://docs.rs#199)#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
[200](https://docs.rs#200)pub struct GzBuilder {
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    extra: Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>,
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    filename: Option<CString>,
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    comment: Option<CString>,
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    // Whether this should be signed is a bit unclear, the gzip spec says mtime is in the unix
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    // time format, which is normally signed, however zlib seems to use an unsigned long for this
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    // field.
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    mtime: u32,
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    os: Option<FileSystemType>,
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    xfl: ExtraFlags,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)}

[284](https://docs.rs#284)    pub fn into_header_with_checksum(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {

[286](https://docs.rs#286)    }
[287](https://docs.rs#287)
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    fn into_header_inner(self, use_crc: bool) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)        let GzBuilder {
[290](https://docs.rs#290)            extra,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)            filename,
[292](https://docs.rs#292)            comment,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            mtime,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            os,
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            xfl,
[296](https://docs.rs#296)        } = self;
[297](https://docs.rs#297)        let os = match os {
[298](https://docs.rs#298)            Some(f) => f,
[299](https://docs.rs#299)            // Set the OS based on the system the binary is compiled for if not set,
[300](https://docs.rs#300)            // as this is a required field.
[301](https://docs.rs#301)            // These defaults are taken from what modern zlib uses, which are not the same as
[302](https://docs.rs#302)            // what's used in flate2.
[303](https://docs.rs#303)            None => {
[304](https://docs.rs#304)                #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[305](https://docs.rs#305)                match env::consts::OS {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)                    "linux" | "freebsd" | "dragonfly" | "netbsd" | "openbsd" | "solaris"
[307](https://docs.rs#307)                    | "bitrig" => FileSystemType::Unix,
[308](https://docs.rs#308)                    "macos" => FileSystemType::Apple,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)                    "win32" => FileSystemType::Tops20OrNTFS,
[310](https://docs.rs#310)                    _ => FileSystemType::Unknown,
[311](https://docs.rs#311)                }
[312](https://docs.rs#312)                #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[313](https://docs.rs#313)                FileSystemType::Unknown
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            }
[315](https://docs.rs#315)        };
[316](https://docs.rs#316)        let mut flg = 0;
[317](https://docs.rs#317)        if use_crc {
[318](https://docs.rs#318)            flg |= FHCRC;
[319](https://docs.rs#319)        };
[320](https://docs.rs#320)        let mut header = alloc::vec![0u8; 10];
[321](https://docs.rs#321)
[322](https://docs.rs#322)        if let Some(v) = extra {
[323](https://docs.rs#323)            flg |= FEXTRA;
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            header.push((v.len()/* >> 0*/) as u8);
[325](https://docs.rs#325)            header.push((v.len() >> 8) as u8);
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            header.extend(v);
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        }
[328](https://docs.rs#328)
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        if let Some(filename) = filename {
[330](https://docs.rs#330)            flg |= FNAME;
[331](https://docs.rs#331)            header.extend(filename.as_bytes_with_nul().iter().cloned());
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        }
[333](https://docs.rs#333)
[334](https://docs.rs#334)        if let Some(comment) = comment {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)            flg |= FCOMMENT;
[336](https://docs.rs#336)            header.extend(comment.as_bytes_with_nul().iter().cloned());
[337](https://docs.rs#337)        }
[338](https://docs.rs#338)
[339](https://docs.rs#339)        header[0] = 0x1f;
[340](https://docs.rs#340)        header[1] = 0x8b;
[341](https://docs.rs#341)        header[2] = 8;
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        header[3] = flg;
[343](https://docs.rs#343)        header[4] = mtime /*>> 0*/ as u8;
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        header[5] = (mtime >> 8) as u8;
[345](https://docs.rs#345)        header[6] = (mtime >> 16) as u8;
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        header[7] = (mtime >> 24) as u8;
[347](https://docs.rs#347)        header[8] = xfl.as_u8();
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        header[9] = os.as_u8();
[349](https://docs.rs#349)
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        if use_crc {
[351](https://docs.rs#351)            let mut crc = Crc::new();
[352](https://docs.rs#352)            crc.update(&header);
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            let checksum = crc.sum() as u16;
[354](https://docs.rs#354)            header.extend(&[checksum as u8, (checksum >> 8) as u8]);
[355](https://docs.rs#355)        }
[356](https://docs.rs#356)
[357](https://docs.rs#357)        header
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    }
[359](https://docs.rs#359)}
[360](https://docs.rs#360)
[361](https://docs.rs#361)/// A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.
[362](https://docs.rs#362)///
[363](https://docs.rs#363)/// The header can contain metadata about the file that was compressed, if
[364](https://docs.rs#364)/// present.
[365](https://docs.rs#365)#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
[366](https://docs.rs#366)pub struct GzHeader {
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    extra: Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>,
[368](https://docs.rs#368)    filename: Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>,
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    comment: Option<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>,
[370](https://docs.rs#370)    mtime: u32,
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    os: u8,
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    xfl: u8,
[373](https://docs.rs#373)}
[374](https://docs.rs#374)
[375](https://docs.rs#375)impl GzHeader {
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    /// Returns the `filename` field of this gzip header, if present.
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    ///
[378](https://docs.rs#378)    /// The `filename` field the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
[379](https://docs.rs#379)    /// encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.

[382](https://docs.rs#382)    }
[383](https://docs.rs#383)

[387](https://docs.rs#387)    }
[388](https://docs.rs#388)
[389](https://docs.rs#389)    /// Returns the `comment` field of this gzip stream's header, if present.
[390](https://docs.rs#390)    ///
[391](https://docs.rs#391)    /// The `comment` field in the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)

[397](https://docs.rs#397)    /// Returns the `mtime` field of this gzip header.
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    ///
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    /// This gives the most recent modification time of the contained file, or alternatively
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// the timestamp of when the file was compressed if the data did not come from a file, or
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// a timestamp was not available when compressing. The time is specified the Unix format,
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    /// that is: seconds since 00:00:00 GMT, Jan. 1, 1970. (Not that this may cause problems for
[403](https://docs.rs#403)    /// MS-DOS and other systems that use local rather than Universal time.)
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    /// An `mtime` value of 0 means that the timestamp is not set.
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    pub const fn mtime(&self) -> u32 {
[406](https://docs.rs#406)        self.mtime
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    }
[408](https://docs.rs#408)
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    /// Returns the `mtime` field of this gzip header as a `SystemTime` if present.
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    ///
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    /// Returns `None` if the `mtime` is not set, i.e 0.
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    /// See [`mtime`](#method.mtime) for more detail.
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    pub fn mtime_as_datetime(&self) -> Option<time::SystemTime> {
[415](https://docs.rs#415)        if self.mtime == 0 {
[416](https://docs.rs#416)            None
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        } else {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)            let duration = time::Duration::new(u64::from(self.mtime), 0);
[419](https://docs.rs#419)            let datetime = time::UNIX_EPOCH + duration;
[420](https://docs.rs#420)            Some(datetime)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        }
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    }
[423](https://docs.rs#423)

[473](https://docs.rs#473)        "corrupt gzip stream does not have a matching header checksum",

[476](https://docs.rs#476)
[477](https://docs.rs#477)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[478](https://docs.rs#478)fn bad_header() -> io::Error {
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "invalid gzip header")
[480](https://docs.rs#480)}
[481](https://docs.rs#481)
[482](https://docs.rs#482)/// Try to read a little-endian u16 from the provided reader.
[483](https://docs.rs#483)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[484](https://docs.rs#484)fn read_le_u16<R: Read>(r: &mut R) -> io::Result<u16> {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    let mut b = [0; 2];
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    r.read_exact(&mut b)?;
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    Ok((b[0] as u16) | ((b[1] as u16) << 8))
[488](https://docs.rs#488)}
[489](https://docs.rs#489)
[490](https://docs.rs#490)/// Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.
[491](https://docs.rs#491)///
[492](https://docs.rs#492)/// Returns a `GzHeader` with the fields filled out if sucessful, or an `io::Error` with
[493](https://docs.rs#493)/// `ErrorKind::InvalidInput` if decoding of the header.
[494](https://docs.rs#494)///
[495](https://docs.rs#495)/// Note that a gzip steam can contain multiple "members". Each member contains a header,
[496](https://docs.rs#496)/// followed by compressed data and finally a checksum and byte count.
[497](https://docs.rs#497)/// This method will only read the header for the "member" at the start of the stream.
[498](https://docs.rs#498)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[499](https://docs.rs#499)pub fn read_gz_header<R: Read>(r: &mut R) -> io::Result<GzHeader> {
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    let mut crc_reader = CrcReader::new(r);
[501](https://docs.rs#501)    let mut header = [0; 10];
[502](https://docs.rs#502)    crc_reader.read_exact(&mut header)?;
[503](https://docs.rs#503)
[504](https://docs.rs#504)    // `ID1` and `ID2` are fixed values to identify a gzip file.
[505](https://docs.rs#505)    let id1 = header[0];
[506](https://docs.rs#506)    let id2 = header[1];
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    if id1 != 0x1f || id2 != 0x8b {
[508](https://docs.rs#508)        return Err(bad_header());
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    }
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    // `CM` describes the compression method. Currently only method 8 (DEFLATE) is specified.
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    // by the gzip format.
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    let cm = header[2];
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    if cm != 8 {
[514](https://docs.rs#514)        return Err(bad_header());
[515](https://docs.rs#515)    }
[516](https://docs.rs#516)
[517](https://docs.rs#517)    // `FLG` the bits in this field indicates whether the `FTEXT`, `FHCRC`, `FEXTRA`, `FNAME` and
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    // `FCOMMENT` fields are present in the header.
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    let flg = header[3];
[520](https://docs.rs#520)    let mtime = (header[4] as u32/* << 0*/)
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        | ((header[5] as u32) << 8)
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        | ((header[6] as u32) << 16)
[523](https://docs.rs#523)        | ((header[7] as u32) << 24);
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    // `XFL` describes the compression level used by the encoder. (May not actually
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    // match what the encoder used and has no impact on decompression.)
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    let xfl = header[8];
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    // `os` describes what type of operating system/file system the file was created on.
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    let os = header[9];
[529](https://docs.rs#529)
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    let extra = if flg & FEXTRA != 0 {
[531](https://docs.rs#531)        // Length of the FEXTRA field.
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        let xlen = read_le_u16(&mut crc_reader)?;
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        let mut extra = alloc::vec![0; xlen as usize];
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        crc_reader.read_exact(&mut extra)?;
[535](https://docs.rs#535)        Some(extra)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    } else {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        None
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    };
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    let filename = if flg & FNAME != 0 {
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        // wow this is slow
[541](https://docs.rs#541)        let mut b = alloc::vec::Vec::new();
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        for byte in crc_reader.by_ref().bytes() {
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            let byte = byte?;
[544](https://docs.rs#544)            if byte == 0 {
[545](https://docs.rs#545)                break;
[546](https://docs.rs#546)            }
[547](https://docs.rs#547)            b.push(byte);
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        }
[549](https://docs.rs#549)        Some(b)
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    } else {
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        None
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    };
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    let comment = if flg & FCOMMENT != 0 {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        // wow this is slow
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        let mut b = alloc::vec::Vec::new();
[556](https://docs.rs#556)        for byte in crc_reader.by_ref().bytes() {
[557](https://docs.rs#557)            let byte = byte?;
[558](https://docs.rs#558)            if byte == 0 {
[559](https://docs.rs#559)                break;
[560](https://docs.rs#560)            }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)            b.push(byte);
[562](https://docs.rs#562)        }
[563](https://docs.rs#563)        Some(b)
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    } else {
[565](https://docs.rs#565)        None
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    };
[567](https://docs.rs#567)
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    // If the `FHCRC` flag is set, the header contains a two-byte CRC16 checksum of the header bytes
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    // that needs to be validated.
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    if flg & FHCRC != 0 {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        let calced_crc = crc_reader.crc().sum() as u16;
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        let stored_crc = read_le_u16(&mut crc_reader)?;
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        if calced_crc != stored_crc {
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            return Err(corrupt());
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        }
[576](https://docs.rs#576)    }
[577](https://docs.rs#577)
[578](https://docs.rs#578)    Ok(GzHeader {
[579](https://docs.rs#579)        extra,
[580](https://docs.rs#580)        filename,
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        comment,
[582](https://docs.rs#582)        mtime,
[583](https://docs.rs#583)        os,
[584](https://docs.rs#584)        xfl,
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    })
[586](https://docs.rs#586)}
[587](https://docs.rs#587)
[588](https://docs.rs#588)#[cfg(test)]
[589](https://docs.rs#589)mod tests {
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    extern crate std;
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    use super::*;
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    use std::io::Cursor;
[593](https://docs.rs#593)
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    fn roundtrip_inner(use_crc: bool) {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        const COMMENT: &[u8] = b"Comment";
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        const FILENAME: &[u8] = b"Filename";
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        const MTIME: u32 = 12345;
[598](https://docs.rs#598)        const OS: FileSystemType = FileSystemType::NTFS;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        const XFL: ExtraFlags = ExtraFlags::FastestCompression;
[600](https://docs.rs#600)
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        let header = GzBuilder::new()
[602](https://docs.rs#602)            .comment(COMMENT)
[603](https://docs.rs#603)            .filename(FILENAME)
[604](https://docs.rs#604)            .mtime(MTIME)
[605](https://docs.rs#605)            .os(OS)
[606](https://docs.rs#606)            .xfl(ExtraFlags::FastestCompression)
[607](https://docs.rs#607)            .into_header_inner(use_crc);
[608](https://docs.rs#608)
[609](https://docs.rs#609)        let mut reader = Cursor::new(header.clone());
[610](https://docs.rs#610)
[611](https://docs.rs#611)        let header_read = read_gz_header(&mut reader).unwrap();
[612](https://docs.rs#612)
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        assert_eq!(header_read.comment().unwrap(), COMMENT);
[614](https://docs.rs#614)        assert_eq!(header_read.filename().unwrap(), FILENAME);
[615](https://docs.rs#615)        assert_eq!(header_read.mtime(), MTIME);
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        assert_eq!(header_read.os(), OS.as_u8());
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        assert_eq!(header_read.xfl(), XFL.as_u8());
[618](https://docs.rs#618)    }
[619](https://docs.rs#619)
[620](https://docs.rs#620)    #[test]
[621](https://docs.rs#621)    fn roundtrip() {
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        roundtrip_inner(false);
[623](https://docs.rs#623)    }
[624](https://docs.rs#624)
[625](https://docs.rs#625)    #[test]
[626](https://docs.rs#626)    fn roundtrip_with_crc() {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        roundtrip_inner(true);
[628](https://docs.rs#628)    }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    #[test]
[631](https://docs.rs#631)    fn filesystem_enum() {
[632](https://docs.rs#632)        for n in 0..20 {
[633](https://docs.rs#633)            assert_eq!(n, FileSystemType::from_u8(n).as_u8());
[634](https://docs.rs#634)        }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)
[636](https://docs.rs#636)        for n in 20..(u8::MAX as u16) + 1 {
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            assert_eq!(FileSystemType::from_u8(n as u8), FileSystemType::Unknown);
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        }
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    }

# Crc in gzip_header - Rust

`pub struct Crc { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A wrapper struct containing a CRC checksum in the format used by gzip and the amount of bytes input to it mod 2^32.

# GzHeader in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/gzip_header/struct.GzHeader.html

`pub struct GzHeader { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A structure representing the raw header of a gzip stream.

The header can contain metadata about the file that was compressed, if present.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Returns the `filename` field of this gzip header, if present.

The `filename` field the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.

Returns the `comment` field of this gzip stream’s header, if present.

The `comment` field in the gzip header is supposed to be stored using ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1)
encoding and be zero-terminated if following the specification.

Returns the `mtime` field of this gzip header.

This gives the most recent modification time of the contained file, or alternatively
the timestamp of when the file was compressed if the data did not come from a file, or
a timestamp was not available when compressing. The time is specified the Unix format,
that is: seconds since 00:00:00 GMT, Jan. 1, 1970. (Not that this may cause problems for
MS-DOS and other systems that use local rather than Universal time.)
An `mtime` value of 0 means that the timestamp is not set.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

Crudely display the contents of the header

Note that filename/commend are required to be ISO 8859-1 (LATIN-1) encoded by the spec, however to avoid dragging in dependencies we simply interpret them as UTF-8. This may result in garbled output if the names contain special characters.

# ExtraFlags in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/gzip_header/enum.ExtraFlags.html

```
#[repr(u8)]pub enum ExtraFlags {
    Default = 0,
    MaximumCompression = 2,
    FastestCompression = 4,
}
```
## Expand description

Valid values for the extra flag in the gzip specification.

This is a field to be used by the compression methods. For deflate, which is the only specified compression method, this is a value indicating the level of compression of the contained compressed data. This value does not have to correspond to the actual compression level of the contained data, it’s only a hint that the the encoder may set.

# FileSystemType in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/gzip_header/enum.FileSystemType.html

```
#[repr(u8)]pub enum FileSystemType {
```
## Show 21 variants

    Fat = 0,
    Amiga = 1,
    Vms = 2,
    Unix = 3,
    Vcms = 4,
    AtariTos = 5,
    Hpfs = 6,
    Macintosh = 7,
    Zsystem = 8,
    Cpm = 9,
    Tops20OrNTFS = 10,
    NTFS = 11,
    SmsQdos = 12,
    Riscos = 13,
    Vfat = 14,
    Mvs = 15,
    Beos = 16,
    TandemNsk = 17,
    Theos = 18,
    Apple = 19,
    Unknown = 255,
}## Expand description

An enum describing the different OS types described in the gzip format. See http://www.gzip.org/format.txt (Additionally, the Apple(19) value is defined in the zlib library).

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Fat)

### Fat = 0

MS-DOS/old FAT filesystem

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Amiga)

### Amiga = 1

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Vms)

### Vms = 2

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unix)

### Unix = 3

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Vcms)

### Vcms = 4

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AtariTos)

### AtariTos = 5

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hpfs)

### Hpfs = 6

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Macintosh)

### Macintosh = 7

Used for apple platforms. Newer encoders may use 19 instead for modern systems.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Zsystem)

### Zsystem = 8

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Cpm)

### Cpm = 9

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Tops20OrNTFS)

### Tops20OrNTFS = 10

This is used for Windows/NTFS in zlib newer than 1.2.11, but not in gzip due to following updates to the ZIP format. See https://github.com/madler/zlib/issues/235 and https://github.com/madler/zlib/commit/ce12c5cd00628bf8f680c98123a369974d32df15

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.NTFS)

### NTFS = 11

Used for Windows platforms for older zlib versions and other encoders.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SmsQdos)

### SmsQdos = 12

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Riscos)

### Riscos = 13

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Vfat)

Newer fat filesystems (i.e FAT32).

Modern apple platforms. Defined in the zlib library (see zutil.h)

# read_gz_header in gzip_header - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gzip-header/latest/target-redirect/gzip_header/fn.read_gz_header.html

## Expand description

Try to read a gzip header from the provided reader.

Returns a `GzHeader` with the fields filled out if sucessful, or an `io::Error` with
`ErrorKind::InvalidInput` if decoding of the header.

Note that a gzip steam can contain multiple “members”. Each member contains a header, followed by compressed data and finally a checksum and byte count. This method will only read the header for the “member” at the start of the stream.

---

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [arg](https://docs.rs/macro.arg.html)
- Create an `Arg`

- Allows you to build the `Command`instance from your Cargo.toml at compile time.

- Allows you to pull the authors for the command from your Cargo.toml at
compile time in the form:
`"author1 lastname <author1@example.com>:author2 lastname <author2@example.com>"`

- Allows you to pull the description from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_name.html)- name - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the name from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_version.html)- version - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the version from your Cargo.toml at compile time as
`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH_PKGVERSION_PRE`

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap::Command

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
